name: Over-the-Rhine
summary: Over-the-Rhine sits just north of downtown and grew from 19th-century German immigrant settlement; Visit Cincy notes it is on the National Register of Historic Places and holds the country's largest collection of well-preserved Italianate architecture. Vine and Main streets are lined with restaurants, bars, breweries and boutiques, and Washington Park faces Music Hall. It is the home base for StartupCincy Week (Union Hall, 1311 Vine St) and for Cincinnati Art Week's storefront galleries, and it hosts BLINK's Over-the-Rhine zone.
details: Getting around (Visit Cincy): "On foot: OTR is a very compact and walkable neighborhood." Red Bike stations and the free Connector streetcar serve the neighborhood.

name: Downtown (Central Business District)
summary: Downtown is Cincinnati's compact urban core, centered on Fountain Square, which Visit Cincy calls the city's symbolic center since 1871 (the Tyler Davidson Fountain). The Fountain District around it holds the Contemporary Arts Center, the Aronoff Center, and the main Public Library. Many of the largest hotels are within a few blocks of the square, and the Connector streetcar loops through the district. It is BLINK's Fountain District zone and sits between OTR to the north and The Banks to the south.
details: Visit Cincy: "The Fountain District is totally walkable, stretching just two blocks on each side from the Tyler Davidson Fountain."
notes: Center point: Nominatim result "Fountain Square, Main Street Historic District, Central Business District, Cincinnati, Hamilton County, Ohio, 45210, United States".

name: The Banks
summary: The Banks is the riverfront entertainment district between Great American Ball Park and Paycor Stadium, with Smale Riverfront Park, the National Underground Railroad Freedom Center, the Andrew J. Brady Music Center and views of the Roebling Suspension Bridge. It is a designated DORA district (drinks in the official cup, 11am–1am daily) and sits on top of the Central Riverfront Garage. The Connector's first station is named The Banks, and BLINK's Riverfront zone and drone shows are here.
details: The Banks FAQ: "The plaza (pedestrian-only area) is 21+ on Friday and Saturday evenings from 10:00 p.m. to 2:00 a.m."

name: Findlay Market
summary: Findlay Market, at 1801 Race Street in northern Over-the-Rhine, has operated in the same iron-framed market house since 1855 and is Ohio's oldest surviving municipal market house. The surrounding blocks (Elder, Race and Elm streets) are packed with food merchants, and Jane's outdoor bar sits on the Elm Street side. It anchors BLINK's Findlay Market zone, and the streetcar stops at stations 10 (Elm) and 12 (Race).
details: Market hours: Tuesday–Friday 9 AM–6 PM, Saturday 8 AM–6 PM, Sunday 10 AM–4 PM, Monday CLOSED.

name: Pendleton
summary: Pendleton is the neighborhood on OTR's eastern edge. Ziegler Park (1322 Sycamore St), with a garage beneath its great lawn, straddles Over-the-Rhine and Pendleton, and the Pendleton Art Center at 1310 Pendleton St opens its artist studios to the public on the last Friday of each month (Final Friday).
details: Pendleton Art Center: "Some studios are open daily; some are open by appointment with the artist." Final Friday dates listed on the site: September 25, 2026 (the next falls after Cincy Week).

name: Covington, Kentucky
summary: Covington is across the Ohio River from downtown Cincinnati, linked by the Roebling Suspension Bridge (opened 1867, the precursor to the Brooklyn Bridge). Visit Cincy describes historic buildings, murals, nightlife and many locally owned restaurants, several of them stops on The B-Line bourbon trail. BLINK's Covington zone runs through downtown Covington, where the city creates a pedestrian Entertainment Destination Center with street closures during the festival.

name: MainStrasse Village
summary: MainStrasse Village is a 19th-century German neighborhood in Covington listed on the National Register of Historic Places, a few blocks' walk from the Northern Kentucky Convention Center and the riverfront hotels. It has restaurants, bars and shops around the Goose Girl Fountain, and Goebel Park's Carroll Chimes Bell Tower plays on the hour.

name: Newport, Kentucky
summary: Newport sits across the Ohio River from Cincinnati's east riverfront, reached on foot by the Purple People Bridge. Visit Cincy notes it was established in 1795 and is now known for family attractions like the Newport Aquarium at Newport on the Levee, bourbon at New Riff Distilling and Pensive Distilling Co., and festivals. It is not a program venue, but its riverfront hotels are walkable to The Banks.

name: The Connector (streetcar)
summary: The Connector is an electric-powered streetcar that operates along a 3.6-mile loop connecting Cincinnati's Over-the-Rhine and Banks neighborhoods via the Central Business District. It is free to ride.

name: BLINK is a walking event: park once, see everything
summary: This is a walking event -- Park Once, See Everything!
details:
No. City streets within the BLINK footprint are closed to automobiles. The best way to enjoy BLINK is by foot!

We recommend taking your BLINK visit slower and visiting 1-2 zones during a visit and returning for more than one night!

name: Each night features (mostly) the same art
summary: With a few exceptions, each night will feature the same shows and art installations. The unique attractions may vary each night.
details: Most displays are between 3-8 mins in length and are on a continuous loop, so you can arrive at any time.

notes: As of 2026-09-24 the Maps & Guides page still says the full event map and individual zone maps are "coming soon".

name: Discounted BLINK transit passes (Transit app)
summary: Riders are encouraged to purchase special discounted BLINK passes through the Transit app before traveling.
details: Discounted tickets go on sale Oct. 5 through the Transit app: One-Day BLINK Pass, valid for 24 hours after activation - $2.20; Four-Day BLINK Pass, valid October 8-11 - $8.00; One-Day Group Pass, for up to four people for 24 hours after activation - $8.00. Cash will continue to be accepted onboard Metro buses and at Metro and BCRTA Park & Ride locations at the standard fare. TANK Park & Ride service will be cashless. Tickets are nonrefundable and nontransferable.
notes: In 2022 and 2024 Metro and TANK rides were fare-free during BLINK; in 2026 riders pay, with discounted BLINK passes.
